# 008: Ids are UUID v7 generated by the database

Status: accepted

## Context

This is a project convention, and the original reason was not written down. UUID v7 starts with a millisecond timestamp, so ids sort roughly by creation time.

## Decision

Ids are never integers. PostgreSQL fills them with `uuid_generate_v7()`, a SQL function created by changeset 003, EF marks them as generated on add, and entities set no initial value. The seeded exercise catalog is the exception: its ids are fixed UUID v7 values in the seed data. Tables keyed by their parent and a value have no id of their own.

## Consequences

- Several session queries order by `Id` to mean "newest first", for example the open session and the recent sets. Changing how ids are generated would break them.
- The function only puts a millisecond timestamp in front of random bits, so two ids from the same millisecond have no guaranteed order.
- A new table with an id needs the default in both the changeset and the EF configuration. The SQLite tests rely on a substitute function ([002](002-sqlite-for-tests.md)).
